note: Cocristalli dye-volatile di cis-azobenzene: (cis-azo)(diossano) e (cis-azo)(pirazina). Tre risposte alla luce che dipendono dall'intensita' (cambio di colore, flessione fotomeccanica, fotoincisione 'cold photocarving'), piu' la loro termica. Il cambio di colore e la flessione sono isomerizzazione parziale cis → trans (conversione misurata con 19F NMR dopo dissoluzione): eventi con a = «reazione» e natura chimica. La fotoincisione (taglio) ha prodotto solido trans-azo I/II (PXRD) e perdita del coformero. Il testo non dà nessun CCDC, gruppo spaziale o cella: forme senza questi dati. Distanze I···O 2.854(2) Å (RXB 0.815) in (cis-azo)(diossano) e I···N 2.896(5) Å (RXB 0.820) in (cis-azo)(pirazina), contro 2.981(3) Å (RXB 0.852) e 2.840(3) Å (RXB 0.805) nei cocristalli trans già noti (rif. 37, 39). Il segnale a circa 52 °C nel DSC di (cis-azo)(pirazina) è la fusione di un po' di pirazina solida (Fig. 5a): non è una forma del colorante, non è un evento. I calcoli (DFT periodica: ΔEiso, ΔEdec, EXB) sono solo in molecole.proprieta (calcolato: true). Per i cocristalli con coformero volatile si segue la regola degli ospiti: il diossano (solvente di cristallizzazione, «a solution of cis-azo in dioxane») è in ospite e la forma e' un solvato, benché gli autori scrivano «cocrystal»; la pirazina (solida, «melting point of a small amount of solid pyrazine» a 52 °C) è un coformero in componenti. Intensità di luce: non esiste un campo per l'irradianza; si usa luce.dose con tipo 'intensita' (mW cm–2, W mm–2) e il diametro del fascio in condizioni.altro. Incoerenze del testo: (1) polvere di (cis-azo)(diossano) con LED: testo «PXRD analysis after 20 min irradiation», didascalia Fig. 2a «before and after 2 h irradiation»; il cristallo singolo: «irradiating a single crystal ... for 20 min ... approximately 8%» ma poi «~8% conversion observed for the photochromic effect observed after 2 h irradiation»; (2) la polvere di (cis-azo)(diossano) dà «a small amount of solid cis-azo» (PXRD) mentre per la pirazina «Similar to (cis-azo)(dioxane), analysis of the PXRD patterns did not reveal any sign of (trans-azo)(pyrazine) or solid cis-azo»; (3) intensita' LED: «approximately 37 mW cm–2 output power at the source» contro «low power intensities (below 1 mW cm–2) generated using the LED light source»; (4) hot-stage: nessuna variazione visibile «until 104 °C» contro l'endoterma DSC di perdita del diossano a 80–110 °C; fusione di trans-azo a 197 °C (DSC) contro «185 °C» (microscopia, «expected melting point»); liquefazione a ~121 °C contro 141 °C (DSC) per cis-azo; (5) Metodi: «For cocrystallization of (trans-azo)(dioxane)» ma i cristalli ottenuti sono (cis-azo)(dioxane) (soluzione irradiata); (cis-azo)(pirazina): risultati «preground equimolar mixture of trans-azo and pyrazine», Metodi 0.010 mmol di trans-azo e 0.075 mmol di pirazina in esano, senza macinazione; (6) «5 C° min–1» (unita' rovinata); «Supplmentary Figure 16» (refuso); «dI···NRB»; (7) confocale: foro grande con «>5 mW ... ∼5 W mm–2», camera veloce: 5 mW ≈ 2.1 W mm–2 (fascio di 78 μm) con solo «minor etching»: setup diversi.

citazioni: Specifically, irradiation at low power intensities (below 1 mW cm–2) generated using the LED light source led only to a change in color (Figure 1c) of the single crystal, which was assignable to the isomerization of cis- to trans-azo.
Irradiation at the lowest light intensity was achieved using a 532 nm dispersed light-emitting diode (LED) of approximately 37 mW cm–2 output power at the source, placed 10 cm away from the crystal.

The extent of isomerization was estimated by irradiating a single crystal of (cis-azo)(dioxane) using the 532 nm LED source for 20 min, followed by dissolution in CDCl3 and 19F nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR) analysis.

Analogous analysis of a nonirradiated (cis-azo)(dioxane) crystal from the same batch revealed no signal of the trans-isomer (Supplementary Figure 8), indicating that the color change upon LED irradiation is associated with approximately 8% extent of cis → trans isomerization.

citazioni: Finally, switching to a laser beam of 78 μm diameter and light intensity of 2.25 W mm–2 resulted in cold photocarving (Figure 1e, also Supporting Information Video 2), evident by clean cutting of the crystal.
In contrast to irradiation at lower power densities, which led to a change in color throughout the crystal, in this case, the color change from yellow to red was only observed on the irradiated spot.

Analysis by PXRD (Figure 2b,c) of a single crystal of (cis-azo)(dioxane) that was cut using a higher light intensity (78 μm beam diameter) 532 nm laser beam, and then placed on a zero-background silicon sample holder, demonstrated the presence of trans-azo polymorphs I and II along with residual (cis-azo)(dioxane).

In contrast, the CPC behavior enabled through the dye-volatile cocrystal design does not involve high-temperature disruption of covalent bonds but instead gentle, low-temperature, and localized cleavage of noncovalent interactions, such as halogen bonds (XB).46

citazioni: Both the isomerization and dioxane loss from the crystal were probed on a confocal Raman microscope using a sequence of two rapid pulses (0.1 s each) of laser light of 532 nm wavelength and 0.1 mW power.

After the first 532 nm pulse, the Raman signals associated with the cis-azo component disappeared completely, concomitant with the appearance of new Raman bands associated with trans-azo. Importantly, the characteristic ν(C–O–C) Raman band for dioxane at 830 cm–1 remained, suggesting that irradiation induced a rapid transformation of (cis-azo)(dioxane) to the corresponding (trans-azo)(dioxane) cocrystal.

citazioni: Photocarving was also studied visually, using a 78 μm beam diameter laser at powers of 5–15 mW (2.1–6.3 W mm–2) and a high-speed camera operating at 1000 frames per second (fps) (Supplementary Figures 13–15).

While irradiation at the low power setting of 5 mW resulted only in minor etching of the cocrystal surface accompanied by a color change, the higher irradiation powers of 10 and 15 mW both resulted in photocarving, clearly evident by the formation of a hole in the crystal surface (Supporting Information Videos 3, 4, and 5).
In each case irradiation led to the emission of a “fog” from the spot of the irradiation, which was assigned to the release of dioxane.37

citazioni: Irradiation with low-intensity 532 nm LED light led to a change in color from yellow to orange (Figure 4c), along with minor cracking of the crystal, attributed to the strain of cis–trans isomerization.
After dissolving the irradiated cocrystal in CDCl3, 19F NMR analysis revealed that cis- to trans-azo conversion took place to an extent of ∼8% (Supplmentary Figure 16).

Notably, such conversion was achieved after 2 h of irradiation, indicating greater photostability of (cis-azo)(pyrazine) compared to (cis-azo)(dioxane) which showed similar conversion after only 20 min of irradiation.

citazioni: Cold photocarving was demonstrated by exposure to either green or blue light, on both fresh or previously irradiated crystals.

Using a sample of (cis-azo)(pyrazine), the sample was exposed to 532 nm laser radiation, showing the ability to readily carve through the crystal using a higher light intensity beam of 2.25 W mm–2 (Figure 4e, also Supporting Information Video 7).

In contrast to their dioxane counterpart, crystals of (cis-azo)(pyrazine) were found to retain crystallinity after cutting with a 532 nm laser beam, which was evident from full X-ray diffraction data that were collected from a parent (cis-azo)(pyrazine) single crystal before irradiation and on the daughter crystal resulting from cutting (Figure 4b, Supplementary Figures 17 and 18).

The freshly laser-cut crystal exhibited only X-ray diffraction signals of (cis-azo)(pyrazine), with the only indication of cis → trans isomerization being a slight change in the color of the cut crystal surface from yellow to red.
eventi.note: Negativo sulla fase: il cristallo tagliato dal laser (taglio completo) resta (cis-azo)(pirazina) all'SCXRD, con solo un lieve cambio di colore sulla superficie di taglio; il taglio avviene (fotoincisione) ma il cristallo figlio non cambia fase. a = ignota perche' il testo non nomina la forma attesa (il confronto e' col diossano, che da' trans-azo I/II).

citazioni: Changes to (cis-azo)(pyrazine) upon irradiation were also followed by PXRD (Supplementary Figure 19), by irradiating a bulk crystalline powder of the cocrystal with dispersed green (532 nm wavelength) LED light of light intensity 37 mW·cm–2.

Visual inspection of the PXRD patterns of the material before and after irradiation indicated the complete transformation of (cis-azo)(pyrazine) to a physical mixture of solids trans-azo I and II over a period of 20 h, demonstrating improved photostability compared to (cis-azo)(dioxane).

Similar to (cis-azo)(dioxane), analysis of the PXRD patterns did not reveal any sign of (trans-azo)(pyrazine) or solid cis-azo, suggesting that cis → trans isomerization and loss of coformer upon irradiation of the (cis-azo)(pyrazine) cocrystal either are simultaneous or occur through intermediates that are too minute to be observed via PXRD.

gruppi_coinvolti.citazione: The light-induced color change and photomechanical bending occur due to different extents of the dye cis → trans isomerization taking place at different irradiation intensities, while the photocarving effect is due the combination of the volatility of the cocrystal former and the photochromic nature of the azobenzene.

The calculated halogen-bonding energies additionally highlight the stability of the pyrazine cocrystals compared to their dioxane counterparts and suggest that the increase in halogen-bonding strength upon switching from an oxygen-based to a nitrogen-based acceptor contributes to the overall stability of the cocrystal.

citazioni: The DSC thermogram for (cis-azo)(dioxane) heated at a rate of 5 C° min–1 shows an endothermic process in the 80–110 °C range, attributed to dioxane loss (Figure 5a).

This assignment was supported by TGA, which revealed a 14.2% loss of weight in the same thermal range, consistent with the theoretically calculated content of dioxane (13.2%) in (cis-azo)(dioxane) (Supplementary Figure 21).
The samples were placed in alumina crucibles, and measurements were conducted under a stream of nitrogen (50 cm3 min–1) gas, at a heating rate of 5 °C min–1.

The DSC, TGA, and hot-stage microscopy show that the first step in the heat-driven process is desolvation of the cocrystal to form solid cis-azo which subsequently melts and then undergoes isomerization and crystallization to form solid trans-azo.

Heating of a yellow (cis-azo)(dioxane) crystal did not produce visible changes in shape or color until 104 °C, when the crystal begins to darken and crack, which was interpreted as due to the loss of dioxane coformer.

While the initial Raman spectrum (25 °C) revealed only bands of cis-azo and dioxane (ν(C–O–C) at 830 cm–1), increasing the temperature to 105 °C led to the appearance of new low-frequency bands (<150 cm–1), indicating changes in intermolecular vibrations, and the disappearance of the dioxane Raman band at 830 cm–1.

gruppi_coinvolti.citazione: Indeed, if the heating is conducted with a (cis-azo)(dioxane) cocrystal submerged in oil, the darkening of the crystal is associated with the appearance of bubbles on the crystal surface, consistent with the removal of gaseous dioxane.

eventi.note: Percorso termico, primo passo: perdita del diossano che da' cis-azo solido (DSC 80–110 °C a 5 °C min–1, TGA 14.2%). Microscopia a stadio caldo (20 °C min–1): il cristallo scurisce e si fessura a 104 °C; Raman in temperatura (cristallo singolo): a 105 °C scompare la banda del diossano a 830 cm–1. Crogiolo: allumina (non si dice se con coperchio), campione 'bulk'. Il DSC alternativo del TA (1 °C min–1, pentola di alluminio ermetica) non e' assegnato a una figura. La microscopia dice nessuna variazione visibile fino a 104 °C mentre il DSC mostra la perdita gia' da 80 °C (incoerenza notata nell'articolo).

citazioni: Further heating leads to another endothermic event at 141 °C, immediately followed by an exothermic process, which has been interpreted as the melting of cis-azo followed by thermally induced isomerization and crystallization into solid trans-azo.32

Further heating leads to liquefaction at ∼121 °C, followed by recrystallization at ∼139 °C to form crystallites of trans-azo that subsequently melt at the expected melting point temperature of 185 °C.
Further heating to 165 °C leads also to the appearance of new Raman bands that were consistent with trans-azo.
The samples were placed in alumina crucibles, and measurements were conducted under a stream of nitrogen (50 cm3 min–1) gas, at a heating rate of 5 °C min–1.

eventi.note: Il cis-azo solido (dal cocristallo desolvato) fonde a 141 °C (DSC) e dal fuso cristallizza trans-azo isomerizzato (esotermo subito dopo): «has been interpreted as» (rif. 32), certezza media. Microscopia: liquefazione a ~121 °C e ricristallizzazione a ~139 °C; Raman: bande del trans-azo a 165 °C. Stessa trasformazione con altre tecniche e T diverse (121 contro 141 °C): un solo evento. Il polimorfo di trans-azo non e' detto: F8.

citazioni: Upon further heating, the DSC thermogram exhibits a sharp endothermic process at 197 °C, consistent with the melting of trans-azo.
The samples were placed in alumina crucibles, and measurements were conducted under a stream of nitrogen (50 cm3 min–1) gas, at a heating rate of 5 °C min–1.
eventi.conflitto: Microscopia a stadio caldo: i cristalliti di trans-azo fondono a 185 °C, «the expected melting point temperature». Si tiene il DSC (197 °C), piu' dettagliato.

citazioni: The DSC analysis of bulk (cis-azo)(pyrazine) (Figure 5a) revealed three distinct endothermic events, the first between 80 and 115 °C, which was identified as loss of pyrazine coformer (confirmed by TGA, which revealed a mass loss of ∼12.5%, Supplementary Figure 24), the second at 140 °C, which was assigned as cis-azo melt, and the third was at 196 °C, which was assigned to the melting of trans-azo.

The two experiments yielded very similar results, with the crystal retaining the overall appearance until ∼90 °C, followed by darkening and the appearance of bubbles (in the case of the crystal submerged in oil) at higher temperatures. These observations are consistent with cis → trans isomerization and thermal loss of pyrazine.
eventi.note: Prima endoterma del DSC di (cis-azo)(pirazina): perdita di pirazina (TGA ~12.5%). Il prodotto e' cis-azo solido solo per via implicita: la seconda endoterma a 140 °C «was assigned as cis-azo melt». Velocita' di riscaldamento non scritta per la pirazina (Fig. 5a sovrappone i due DSC; il metodo dichiara 5 °C min–1 per il sistema TGA/DSC e 1 °C min–1 per il TA). Il segnale debole a ~52 °C e' la fusione di pirazina solida in eccesso (Fig. 5a), non un evento della forma.

citazioni: After each pulse, the Raman spectrum of the irradiated spot on the crystal was immediately recorded using a 785 nm red laser, previously verified not to elicit a photoresponse.

The type of photoresponse was not noticeably dependent on the wavelength of incident irradiation (488, 515, or 532 nm), as long as either green or blue light was used, i.e. light with wavelengths that can excite well within the n−π* absorption band of the azo component (Supplementary Figure 3).
eventi.note: Il laser rosso a 785 nm usato come sonda Raman, «previously verified not to elicit a photoresponse»: nessuna risposta (la verifica non e' mostrata nel testo; intensita' e durata non dette). La risposta c'e' solo con luce verde o blu, nella banda n−π* del gruppo azo.

preparazioni.pretrattamento: soluzione di trans-azo irradiata 30 min con LED a 532 nm (37 mW·cm–2) per ottenere il cis-azo
citazioni: Yellow needle-shaped single crystals of (cis-azo)(dioxane) were obtained by slow evaporation of a solution of cis-azo in dioxane.

For cocrystallization of (trans-azo)(dioxane) approximately 6 mg of trans-azo (0.010 mmol) was dissolved in a minimal volume of 1,4-dioxane (∼2 mL). The solution was then irradiated for 30 min via a 532 nm 37 mW·cm–2 LED and left to evaporate at room temperature, yielding long, yellow, needle-shaped crystals.
preparazioni.conflitto: I Metodi intitolano la prova «cocrystallization of (trans-azo)(dioxane)», ma i cristalli ottenuti dalla soluzione irradiata sono (cis-azo)(dioxane) (Risultati).
preparazioni.note: Il cis-azo si forma in soluzione per irraggiamento del trans-azo e poi cristallizza con il diossano.

preparazioni.pretrattamento: soluzione irradiata con LED a 532 nm (37 mW·cm–2) per formare cis-azo
citazioni: Crystals of (cis-azo)(pyrazine) were readily obtained by the crystallization of a preground equimolar mixture of trans-azo and pyrazine. The sample was then dissolved in hexanes with dropwise addition of CH2Cl2 until complete dissolution. The resulting solution was irradiated by a 532 nm LED source to induce the formation of cis-azo and left to crystallize by slow evaporation.

For cocrystallization of (cis-azo)(pyrazine), approximately 6 mg of trans-azo (0.010 mmol) and 6 mg of pyrazine (0.075 mmol) were mixed in hexanes (∼5 mL) with methylene chloride added dropwise until all material was fully dissolved. The solution was then irradiated with a 532 nm 37 mW·cm–2 LED. The solution was left to evaporate at room temperature, yielding lath-shaped yellow crystals.
preparazioni.conflitto: Risultati: «preground equimolar mixture of trans-azo and pyrazine»; Metodi: 0.010 mmol di trans-azo e 0.075 mmol di pirazina mescolati in esano, senza macinazione. Cristalli «large plates» nei Risultati, «lath-shaped» nei Metodi.
